meta.title: ManyDesk — Free, open-source remote desktop without servers
meta.description: ManyDesk is a free, open-source remote desktop for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android. Peer-to-peer and end-to-end encrypted, with no account and no server in the middle.
og.image.alt: The ManyDesk logo and the words: Remote desktop without servers.
ld.features: Remote desktop control, file transfer, remote terminal, voice and camera, clipboard sync, unattended access with TOTP, LAN discovery, Wake-on-LAN, end-to-end encryption
hero.lead: Fast, end-to-end encrypted, peer-to-peer remote access for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android. No account. No cloud in the middle. Open source.
latest: Latest version: {v} · Free and open source
soon: First release coming soon · build from source today
pill.lan: Works without internet on the LAN
modes.title: Exactly the access you need
modes.sub: Open the full desktop, or connect for files or a terminal alone. The last two never capture the screen, and the host grants only what that session needs.
modes.d.title: See and control
modes.d.text: Multi-monitor, voice, cameras, chat, clipboard and file transfer, whiteboard, remote restart and privacy mode.
modes.f.title: Just the files
modes.f.text: A two-pane file manager to move files and folders both ways, without showing the remote screen.
modes.t.title: Just a shell
modes.t.text: A full terminal on the remote computer: your login shell on macOS and Linux, PowerShell on Windows.
feat.title: Everything you expect. Nothing in between.
feat.sub: ManyDesk follows the workflow people already know from AnyDesk — a 9-digit address, an accept button — and adds what a serverless design makes possible.
f1.p: Hardware H.264, a dedicated stream per frame and adaptive quality. An idle screen costs almost no bandwidth.
f2.p: Password with optional TOTP two-factor and trusted devices. On Windows, reachable even at the sign-in screen.
f3.p: Text, rich text, images, files and folders in both directions. Copy files here, paste them over there.
f4.p: Finds computers on your LAN, connects without internet, accepts a plain IP and wakes machines with Wake-on-LAN.
f5.p: Talk while you work, see each other on camera, and keep a chat in every session.
f6.p: Switch monitors, change the remote resolution, or add a virtual display to a Mac with no monitor.
f7.p: Each with their own permissions, chat and a color-coded pointer that only the host sees.
f8.p: Ctrl+Alt+Del, remote restart with reconnect, privacy mode, whiteboard, switch sides and TCP tunnels.
how.title: Two computers, one direct line
how.sub: There is no ManyDesk server to sign in to, to pay for or to trust. Computers meet through public networks that already exist, then talk directly.
s1.p: A signed, encrypted request of a few kilobytes travels over 11 Nostr relays, 4 MQTT brokers and your local network at once. Any one of them is enough.
s2.p: Both sides open a direct UDP path through their routers and run QUIC with TLS 1.3 over it. Where no direct path exists, a TURN relay carries the encrypted traffic.
s3.p: The screen is encoded in hardware. Every frame has its own stream, so a lost packet delays one frame, never the ones behind it.
how.diagram: The host and the viewer exchange a short signed and encrypted handshake through Nostr relays, MQTT brokers and the local network. Video, input, audio and files then flow directly between them over QUIC with TLS 1.3.
sec.title: Private by design
sec.sub: Without a server in the middle, there is nobody else who could look in. ManyDesk makes sure of the rest.
c1.p: TLS 1.3 with certificates pinned in both directions for every session.
c2.p: Unattended access is proven with an HMAC over a fresh challenge; the host keeps only a PBKDF2 key.
c3.p: Control, clipboard, files, audio, camera, terminal: each a separate permission, granted per viewer and revocable at any time.
c4.p: Open source under Apache-2.0. Every release ships with checksums and signed build provenance.
sas.p: Both screens show the same six digits, derived from both certificates. If they match, nobody is in the middle.
